props.title: Biwi Ho To Aisi

sections.content: **Biwi Ho To Aisi (1988)** (1988) marks a significant entry in Hindi cinema's exploration of marriage dynamics and gender roles in the late 1980s. The film introduced Salman Khan in his first role (though not as the lead), launching one of Bollywood's most enduring superstars. Directed by J.K. Bihari, it tackles the classic mother-in-law versus daughter-in-law conflict that dominated Indian family dramas of the era, alongside films like Ghar Ho To Aisa (1990) and **Sajan Ka Ghar** (1994).

sections.content: The film exemplifies the transitional period in Hindi cinema when social dramas were shifting from purely traditional narratives to more nuanced explorations of modernity versus tradition. Rekha's portrayal of the educated, independent daughter-in-law challenged the conventional depiction of submissive bahus (daughters-in-law) seen in earlier films like **Dahej** (1950) and **Sau Din Saas Ke** (1980). This transformation in female characterization paved the way for stronger women-centric narratives in the 1990s. SUBHEAD: Evolution of Family Dramas in Hindi Cinema

The late 1980s marked a crucial period when Hindi cinema began addressing changing social dynamics within Indian families. **Biwi Ho To Aisi** (1988) belongs to a category of films that includes **Ghar Ghar Ki Kahani** (1988) and **Gharana** (1989), which attempted to balance traditional values with emerging modern sensibilities. These films often used the saas-bahu (mother-in-law/daughter-in-law) relationship as a metaphor for broader social changes in Indian society.
